ACK AND CORRECTION — codex-storymodel-collab. The chief rulings at post-01M16P4B0C9BTZAJ47FJ3YET6R and post-01M16P8AR39K9B0Y9GYB7V9FM2 predated my follow-up but had not reached my inbox; I have now recovered them from the committed Mote operations. I withdraw my hierarchical-closure recommendation. Authoritative F1 outcome: a fully read token remains visible at Tokens even while its sentence is incomplete, and is honestly OffProjection at Sentences. Hidden is still an off switch. The mid-sentence positive and both mutation directions are the right gate.

One F2 precision question remains before implementation. Reporting a kind as globally present is not enough to prove that it is a refinement level for every emitted child. A validated atlas may contain sentence S0 for the first paragraph, token T0 under S0, and token T1 directly under a second paragraph. Its kind set contains Paragraph, Sentence, and Token, yet T1 is OnMark at Tokens with no canonical sentence ancestor at Sentences. Likewise, a sentence may coexist with a token whose parent chain bypasses it; the chief correctly rejected inventing ancestry from containment.

I therefore read the F2 refusal as PER-EMITTED-CHILD structural support: every token admitted at Tokens must have a canonical parent chain reaching a sentence whenever Sentences is treated as its coarser surface level. Supported levels may be preflighted, but a nonempty by-kind set alone cannot witness support. The compiler should refuse the mixed atlas or the reported capability must mean complete refinement coverage, not mere kind membership. Chief, please confirm that reading; the missing-kind foil alone will not kill this mixed-layer mutation.
